meta.description: Detect allele-specific chromatin accessibility from ATAC-seq using WASP, GATK ASEReadCounter, or RASQUAL. Use when mapping cis-regulatory genetic variants from heterozygous SNPs, validating GWAS variant function with allelic imbalance, building a phased within-peak ASE analysis, or detecting reference-allele mapping bias before downstream analysis.

scientific_integrity.detail: No result invents identifiers, sample sizes, p-values, effect sizes, or validation claims. Numerical assertions were recomputed from deterministic fixtures or the bounded public ENCODE, 1000 Genomes, UCSC, WASP, GATK, and RASQUAL executions.

practice_boundaries.detail: The skill remains a research analysis workflow, distinguishes computational evidence from MPRA or CRISPR validation, and makes no patient-specific diagnosis or treatment recommendation.

methodological_ground.detail: Counts are mapping-bias corrected before inference, target genotypes are selected before heterozygous filtering, alleles are oriented to phased haplotypes, phase sets and genomic peak coordinates define groups, multiplicity is controlled, and underpowered groups are not called balanced.

code_usability.detail: All 15 shipped tests passed with ResourceWarnings promoted to errors; the bounded public WASP-to-GATK workflow completed with validated outputs; and the public two-feature RASQUAL workflow completed with 166 association rows and a matching independent BH recomputation.

functional_suitability.note: The single-sample WASP/GATK branch, phase-aware peak aggregation, bounded moderate-cohort RASQUAL driver, and explicit external routes cover the promised scope without substituting an unshipped cohort model.

reliability.note: Input schemas, sample identity, target genotype, phase sets, duplicate intervals, empty results, staging, and output reuse all fail explicitly or produce stable empty schemas; the standalone aggregate helper writes directly to its requested output rather than staging that one file.

performance_context.note: Progressive references and bounded per-feature drivers avoid unnecessary context and computation, while the mandatory WASP realignment remains inherently expensive but thread-configurable and scientifically necessary.

agent_usability.note: Method routing, exact runnable surfaces, stop conditions, status semantics, postconditions, and external-only boundaries are clear; one must still consult setup and method references before execution as intentionally routed.

human_usability.note: Natural trigger language, explicit defaults, readable output columns and statuses, actionable errors, and safe retry semantics make the workflow discoverable and recoverable.

security.note: No credentials, raw-code evaluation, shell interpolation of untrusted commands, unsafe sample-derived filenames, silent overwrite, or broad destructive operation was found.

maintainability.note: Three focused executables, four routed references, deterministic schemas, and 15 regression tests separate scientific concerns and make the corrected coordinate-identity invariant directly testable.

agent_specific.note: Triggering, progressive disclosure, composable file contracts, non-overwriting runs, and explicit escape hatches are strong; the workflow intentionally depends on several pinned external bioinformatics tools.

inputs.label: Bounded public WASP-to-GATK and coordinate-safe aggregation
inputs.note: The exact candidate completed on bounded ENCODE/1000 Genomes chr1:1-5 Mb data with an explicitly declared PS=1 derivative, while the unmodified PS-free source was rejected and cleaned up.

assertions.text: The pipeline retains exactly the BAM target sample before heterozygous filtering.
assertions.note: The filtered VCF contained only NA12878 and 3,542 target heterozygous variants.

assertions.text: The final WASP BAM is coordinate sorted, sample-read-grouped, indexed, and non-empty.
assertions.note: The final BAM reported SO=coordinate, one NA12878 SM, a readable index, and 268,176 reads.

assertions.text: GATK ASEReadCounter emits non-empty scientifically inspectable rows.
assertions.note: GATK emitted 953 rows, of which 28 met total depth 30.

assertions.text: Peak aggregation uses the declared phased schema and meaningful coordinate-safe values.
assertions.note: The 28 depth-eligible SNPs produced one 28-SNP, non-significant phase-oriented peak row with the exact ten-column schema.

assertions.text: A PS-free public input is rejected without leaving final or staged output.
assertions.note: The source VCF lacking PS failed before promotion and left no final output or temporary sibling.

inputs.label: Coordinate identity, phase orientation, schemas, and labels
inputs.note: The former ASA-009 case now remains two coordinate-distinct rows; phase orientation, phase separation, labels, duplicate-coordinate refusal, stable schemas, and malformed inputs all passed.

assertions.text: Opposite locus-specific REF labels are oriented to one biological haplotype before pooling.
assertions.note: The shared phase block produced haplotype counts 180:20 and significant_imbalance.

assertions.text: Different phase sets remain separate and preserve status semantics.
assertions.note: A second block remained a separate two-SNP non_significant row.

assertions.text: Two disjoint genomic intervals with the same BED4 label cannot be pooled.
assertions.note: The exact prior failure emitted two dup rows, each with snp_count 1 and underpowered_snp_count, with zero significant calls.

assertions.text: Genomic coordinates plus phase set define groups and BED labels remain display-only.
assertions.note: The intersection retained chrAudit:99-150 and chrAudit:199-250; BED3 and BED4 results were identical outside the display column.

assertions.text: Exact duplicate coordinates, malformed ASE data, empty input, and no overlap fail or return schema safely.
assertions.note: Duplicate intervals and malformed counts exited 2 without result files; empty and no-overlap cases returned header-only ten-column tables.

inputs.label: Target genotype, identity, staging, and reuse guards
inputs.note: Synthetic BAM/VCF boundaries and the public run confirmed target-only selection, mismatch refusal, staged cleanup, quoted paths, and non-overwriting retry behavior.

assertions.note: Synthetic pipeline, public pipeline, and RASQUAL reruns all refused existing outputs with their documented errors.

assertions.text: Paths containing spaces survive every tested runnable workflow.
assertions.note: Aggregate, RASQUAL argument arrays, and the complete public WASP/GATK run preserved spaced paths.

inputs.label: Two-feature public RASQUAL execution and global BH correction
inputs.note: The exact driver executed both public matrix rows, emitted 166 finite association rows, and matched an independent BH recomputation over the complete reported family.

assertions.text: Two feature records map to distinct one-based binary-matrix rows.
assertions.note: C11orf21 used row 1 and TSPAN32 used row 2 in dry-run and real output.

assertions.text: The real run produces results for every executable feature.
assertions.note: Each feature produced 83 rows, for 166 association rows total.

assertions.text: Raw and adjusted probabilities are finite and lie within zero and one.
assertions.note: All 332 probability values passed finite-range checks.

assertions.text: BH adjustment covers the complete two-feature test family.
assertions.note: An independent BH recomputation across all 166 raw p-values matched every emitted adjusted value.

assertions.text: Dimension, zero-feature, path-array, and output-reuse boundaries are enforced.
assertions.note: Wrong matrix bytes failed, a zero-feature row was skipped explicitly, argument arrays preserved paths, and existing output was refused.

key_strengths: The public WASP-to-GATK path enforces target sample identity, heterozygous selection order, mapping-bias correction, phase requirements, sorted read-grouped indexed BAM output, non-empty GATK counts, and staged non-overwriting publication.

Peak aggregation orients locus-specific REF/ALT counts to haplotypes and keys statistical groups by genomic coordinates plus phase set, so repeated display labels cannot manufacture pooled significance.
The bounded RASQUAL driver validates matrix dimensions and feature rows, executes without a shell, preserves matrix-row ownership, and applies BH to the complete emitted feature-variant family.
All prior findings ASA-001 through ASA-009 are independently closed by executable evidence, including the exact fixture that previously triggered the methodological veto.
